title: 501(c)(3)
summary: A 501(c)(3) organization is a US nonprofit exempt from federal income tax under Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3). It may be organized as a corporation, trust, or association and must operate exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, literary, educational, or certain other qualifying purposes. Tax exemption is obtained primarily by filing IRS Form 1023, with fees of $850 or $400 depending on expected gross receipts. Some entities, such as churches and very small organizations, may be automatically exempt. Donations to 501(c)(3) organizations may be tax-deductible for donors, but loss of status can be fatal to fundraising. Organizations are classified as either public charities or private foundations based on their funding sources and activities.

mechanisms.title: Tax-exempt purpose limitation
mechanisms.explanation: The organization must be specifically limited in its organizing documents to purposes the IRS classifies as tax-exempt, such as religious, charitable, scientific, or educational activities. This limitation is required in the articles of incorporation or bylaws and is crucial for obtaining and maintaining 501(c)(3) status.

mechanisms.title: IRS filing and fee process
mechanisms.explanation: Most organizations obtain exemption by filing IRS Form 1023, accompanied by an $850 filing fee if expected yearly gross receipts are $10,000 or more, or a $400 fee if below that threshold. Some organizations, including churches and certain small entities, are automatically treated as exempt without filing Form 1023.
